judgments.rationale: The role-independent reading is supported for the selected Q1 antecedent. The answer retains the money, territory, recipient and activity qualifications while expressly making the LC's role immaterial. Attaching the closing phrase to applicability or more locally to conducting Type 13 activity supplies no basis for requiring transfer_agent. The question's Transfer Agent example explains the answer's purpose without restricting its general wording. The candidate appropriately acknowledges that its conjunction is only a controlled abstraction: the declared handling fact does not establish the full recipient/activity relationship. Support for the reading therefore does not validate the vocabulary as a complete legal encoding. Separating Schedule 11 expectations is faithful to Q1 and Q3, provided their distinct wording and conditions remain intact. Q2 concerns commencement of a particular deadline, not an additional universal Q1 exclusion. The supplied execution differences demonstrate the consequences of adding a role dependency; they do not establish English meaning. No parallel-language evidence is supplied.

source_evidence.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, regardless of the role played by such LC.
Would activities that an RA 13 depositary performs in its capacity as a Transfer Agent (TA) (eg, processing payments in designated accounts) be subject to requirements under the CMR?

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).
Generally, the relevant period starts on the day when the receipt1 by the RA 13 LC in Hong Kong becomes scheme money of any relevant CIS.

Where REIT collection or operating accounts are opened in the name of SPVs and the RA 13 LC only operates those accounts in accordance with the management company’s instructions, the monies in those accounts are unlikely to be considered scheme money received or held by the RA 13 LC. The CMR will not apply in these cases, but the RA 13 LC should observe relevant requirements in Schedule 11 in respect of those monies, in particular paragraph 19(b)

judgments.unresolved_question: Can the external classifications establish that the same money is received or held in Hong Kong by the specified LC or its AE in the course of that LC's Type 13 activity without silently strengthening the supplied meaning of ra13_context?

missed_readings: No additional defensible role-sensitive affirmative Q1 trigger is apparent. However, the candidate says rival negation attachments in u19 remain explicit questions without actually specifying them: “not” could negate scheme-money status alone, with Hong Kong receipt or holding qualifying that money, or negate the composite description of scheme money received or held in Hong Kong. This affects the negative statement and the reach of “In such cases”, although it does not alter u18's affirmative trigger.

Q3 u43 combines a qualified classification (“unlikely”) with a categorical consequence (“will not apply in these cases”). Preserve the possible reading that the described account circumstances themselves receive a categorical nonapplication answer, alongside the reading that nonapplication depends on the qualified classification. Neither should silently become a new universal Q1 exclusion.
questions: What incorporated definitions and missing dependency establish scheme-money status and the relevant LC/AE relationship? The packet incorporates legislation but does not supply it.
Does “In such cases” in u19 extend the Schedule 11 expectation to all failures of the composite money-and-territory description, or only to non-scheme money in the stated territorial setting?
How should u43's categorical nonapplication sentence be reconciled with its preceding “unlikely” classification when contrary facts establish receipt or holding?
Does any material AE-role qualification arise from the incorporated provisions? The phrase “such LC” expressly concerns the LC and does not independently resolve every AE-role question.
vocabulary_concerns: ra13_context describes handling, which is broader than receipt or holding. Together with the actor-free in_hong_kong fact, it can fail to connect the receipt or holding to the specified LC or AE and that LC's Type 13 activity. The candidate discloses this gap but does not encode its resolution.

scheme_money relies on incorporated legal definitions under u1; their content is unavailable here. Q3 also combines money classification with attribution of receipt or holding, so those determinations should not be presumed independent.

Unknown receipt in u31 is a substantive classification subject to policy qualifications and contrary evidence, not the runtime UNKNOWN value. The source also requires reasonable tracking and prompt reconciliation; neither follows from the Boolean.

Schedule 11 language varies: u19 says “is expected”, u42 and u43 say “should”, and u43 describes paragraph 19(b) as requiring oversight. Keeping these outside the predicate is appropriate, but a generic reference to duties must not erase those modalities, beneficiaries or conditions.

The statement “Unknown facts remain unknown” needs the runtime qualification that a known false conjunct can determine FALSE despite another unknown input. Likewise, FALSE establishes failure of the supplied conjunction; failure of the full legal antecedent follows only after the abstraction's correspondence is established.

Omitting transfer_agent appropriately represents its irrelevance to this trigger. A complete enumeration of LC roles is unnecessary, but this omission does not establish unrestricted role independence for AEs or other legal requirements.

The Boolean contains no deadline or temporal transition. Q2's “Generally” and u31's “would not normally ... except where there is evidence to the contrary” must remain qualified external classifications rather than categorical exclusions.
